language_wrapper: In a math contest, {alpha} rounds are held. For each positive integer n and real numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n chosen from the interval [-{neg_bound}, {pos_bound}], let S = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n. Define F(n) to be the maximum possible value of sum_{i=1}^n | (S - {t_param}·a_i)/n - a_i | over all such choices of a_1, ..., a_n. Compute the value of sum_{k=1}^{alpha} k·F(k).
hardness_rationale: The seed is symmetric on [-1,1] with a fixed coefficient, leading to a relatively clean extremal pattern. This family introduces asymmetry via bounds [-A,B] with A != B and a coupling parameter t. The extremal analysis still requires convexity arguments, but the lack of symmetry and the additional parameter produce a piecewise-linear optimization over m with multiple regime changes. Solving an instance analytically demands careful casework and structural insight, surpassing the seed’s difficulty. The summation up to alpha aggregates many such regimes, thwarting guesswork and requiring systematic reasoning.
notes:
Proof of correctness and reduction: Let n be fixed. For a_i in [-A,B], define S = sum_i a_i and consider G(a_1,...,a_n) = sum_{i=1}^n | (S - t a_i)/n - a_i |. Each term equals | (1/n) * sum_{j=1}^n a_j - ((t/n)+1) * a_i |, which is the absolute value of an affine function in the vector (a_1,...,a_n). Hence each term is convex, and G, being a sum of convex functions, is convex on the hyperrectangle [-A,B]^n. Maximizing a convex function over a convex compact set achieves its maximum at extreme points of the domain. Therefore, in any maximizer, each a_i is an endpoint, i.e., a_i in {-A, B}. Let m be the number of indices with a_i = B (0 <= m <= n). Then S = m B - (n - m) A = m(A+B) - nA. For any i with a_i = B, the contribution is | (S - t B)/n - B | = | (A + B)(m - n) - t B | / n. For any i with a_i = -A, the contribution is | (S + t A)/n + A | = | m(A + B) + t A | / n. Summing yields, for fixed m,
F_m(n) = (1/n) [ m * | (A+B)(m - n) - t B | + (n - m) * | m(A+B) + t A | ].
Thus F(n) = max_{0 <= m <= n} F_m(n), and since the requested sum is sum_{k=1}^alpha k F(k), we have k F(k) = max_{0 <= m <= k} [ m * | (A+B)(m - k) - t B | + (k - m) * | m(A+B) + t A | ], which is an integer when A,B,t are integers. The verifier implements this reduction exactly, ensuring correctness. The generator enforces nontriviality by requiring many n to have interior maximizers (0 < m < n), which precludes easy endpoint-only cases and raises the challenge. This generalization subsumes the seed: setting A=B=1 and t=1 recovers the original form, but our family excludes the perfectly symmetric case to heighten complexity.
source_question: For positive integer \(n\) and real numbers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \in[-1,1]\). Let \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\) and \(f(n)\) be the maximum value of \(\sum_{i=1}^n\left|\frac{S-a_i}{n}-a_i\right|\). Find \(\sum_{k=1}^{225} kf(k)\)．
